boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UMass Amherst spaces for making, studying, meeting, and taking a campus pause.

cards.title: Cross the bridge at Campus Pond
cards.subtitle: Central campus, Amherst
cards.notes: Use the pond bridge as a direct central-campus crossing, then pause on the shore to watch the fountain and waterfowl.
cards.short_summary: A central pond with a bridge, fountain, and seasonal campus gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass identifies Campus Pond as an on-campus accessible place; its admissions office documents the bridge, fountain, wildlife, and PondFire gatherings.
cards.source_title: Pond Fires Bring the Campus Together
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus destination; event activities vary by date.

cards.entity_name: W. E. B. Du Bois Library
cards.title: Choose a Du Bois study floor
cards.subtitle: 154 Hicks Way, Amherst
cards.notes: Match the work to the floor: the directory identifies quiet-study, group-study, Learning Commons, and Digital Media Lab areas.
cards.short_summary: A 26-floor library with clearly designated quiet and group study options.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s floor directory lists quiet-study and group-study areas, the Learning Commons, and the Digital Media Lab.
cards.source_title: W. E. B. Du Bois Library Floor Directory
cards.access_notes: Check the floor directory and library access information before visiting.

cards.title: Take a break at RECESS
cards.subtitle: Du Bois Library, Floor 2
cards.notes: Stop by the Floor 2 space for a low-key reset; student-centered events may include games, open mic sessions, and crafts.
cards.short_summary: A library space built around relaxing, connecting, and student-centered activities.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Libraries describes RECESS as a Floor 2 space for students to relax, recharge, and connect, with activities including games, open mic, and crafts.
cards.access_notes: The space remains shared during events; student groups may submit booking requests.

cards.title: Make something at the Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Agricultural Engineering Building North, Rooms 120–122
cards.notes: Begin with the posted orientation code, then use available training and staff support to work with tools or prototype an idea.
cards.short_summary: An interdisciplinary fabrication space with equipment, training, and mentorship.
cards.evidence_claim: The Makerspace is open to students across majors and provides space, tools, equipment, training, and connections for makers.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists fall and spring open hours as 10 a.m.–9 p.m. daily; closures apply on holidays and campus closure days.

cards.title: Read among the plants at Durfee
cards.subtitle: 210 Stockbridge Road, Amherst
cards.notes: Visit during weekday open hours and use the conservatory’s garden or Rainforest House seating for a short reading break.
cards.short_summary: A historic plant conservatory with themed houses and student seating.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass says students read in the outside gardens and that the Rainforest House has seating for studying or reading.
cards.access_notes: Official visitor hours are Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; review visitor policies before arrival.

cards.title: Meet in the Student Union
cards.subtitle: 41 Campus Center Way, Amherst
cards.notes: Use the Union as a starting point for student-organization activity, then reserve a meeting room through the student-union process when needed.
cards.short_summary: The campus hub for student organizations, meetings, and shared common areas.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass identifies the Student Union as a building for student organizations and extracurricular activity, with shared common areas and meeting spaces.
cards.access_notes: Meeting rooms require reservation through a UMass email account; check current building hours before going.

cards.title: See an exhibition at UMCA
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Center, Amherst
cards.notes: Walk through the current galleries, then look for student educator, curatorial, internship, or work-study opportunities if you want to participate.
cards.short_summary: UMass’s teaching museum for contemporary-art exhibitions and student involvement.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass describes UMCA as its teaching museum and says admission is always free, with student educator, curatorial, internship, and work-study opportunities.
cards.source_title: Art Museums at UMass: University Museum of Contemporary Art
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Tuesday–Friday and weekend hours, plus first-Thursday evening hours; it is closed Mondays, breaks, and state holidays.

cards.title: Check the Old Chapel calendar
cards.subtitle: 144 Hicks Way, Amherst
cards.notes: Look for a public lecture, workshop, or performance in the Great Hall, and allow walking time because there is no adjacent parking.
cards.short_summary: A restored historic campus building that hosts events in several spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass describes Old Chapel as a central-campus event destination with a Great Hall and multipurpose room.
cards.access_notes: Event spaces are scheduled or booked; verify the calendar and event-specific entry details before visiting.

cards.title: Use the Rec Center as a group reset
cards.subtitle: 161 Commonwealth Avenue, Amherst
cards.notes: Coordinate a workout, group class, pickup game, or post-exercise lounge break, then confirm that your UCard or membership allows access.
cards.short_summary: A campus wellness facility with fitness areas, courts, studios, track, and lounge space.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass lists fitness areas, group classes, recreational sports, courts, an indoor track, and lounge space at the Recreation Center.
cards.access_notes: A valid UCard or Rec Center membership is required for fitness areas; operating hours are subject to change.

cards.entity_name: Science and Engineering Library Learning Studio
cards.title: Collaborate in the SEL Learning Studio
cards.subtitle: Science and Engineering Library, Amherst
cards.notes: Use the Learning Studio when a project needs a flexible, multimedia-equipped setting rather than a silent individual-study area.
cards.short_summary: A configurable library space for student collaboration and multimedia work.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Libraries describes the Science and Engineering Library Learning Studio as flexible space for multimedia-equipped classes, events, and collaborative student work.
cards.source_title: Dean’s Message to UMass Families, Fall 2021
cards.access_notes: Confirm current library access and any room-use requirements before planning a group session.
